newsitem.title: FRANCE: MOTOR RACING-PROST CONFIDENT ABOUT LIGIER TAKEOVER.
newsitem.headline: MOTOR RACING-PROST CONFIDENT ABOUT LIGIER TAKEOVER.

text.p: Former Formula One world champion Alain Prost said he was confident and optimistic about his plan to take over constructor Ligier but nothing had yet been signed with current owner Flavio Briatore.

"Right now we are finalising our agreement with Flavio Briatore but the case is not over yet," the four times world champion told sports daily l'Equipe. "It is very likely that it will happen but no deal has yet been definitely signed."
Sunday paper Le Journal du Dimanche reported that the purchase had already taken place and that the team, to be called "Prost Grand Prix" would be equipped by a Peugeot engine for the 1998 season.
But Prost said: "I have no contract with Peugeot. I hope to get one and I'm confident about it, which is different."
Rumours that Prost was about to take over Ligier have been circulating for months. The French sports ministry said last year it supported the idea of a fully French Formula One team headed by Prost.
